title: `split_part(s, t, 1)`: the prefix before the leftmost `t`, the first code point for an empty `t`
verdict: `sverify_split_first` for `t ≠ ''`; for `t = ''` the first code point, `''` for `''`
description: `split_part(s, t, 1)` is the part of `s` before the leftmost occurrence of `t`, or `s` where `t` does not occur, counted in characters on non-ASCII text, with `t` read literally (`.` and `%` are not patterns). A NULL `s` or `t` gives NULL.

An empty `t` splits `s` into its code points, so the first part is the first code point: `'日本'` gives `'日'`, `'😀a'` `'😀'`, `'éx'` written as the single code point U+00E9 gives `'é'` whole, and `'éx'` written as `e` followed by U+0301 (a combining acute) gives `'e'`: code points, not graphemes. An empty `s` gives `''`.

The native call returns on every one of these inputs, an empty pattern included: it raises nowhere and gives a value or NULL (ruling 290's P6), so a lowering that evaluates it there and discards the value is safe.
reference: `sverify_split_first(s, t)` (`Text.splitFirst`, ruling 286) is the prefix before the leftmost `t`, `s` where `t` does not occur, and `s` for an empty `t`. The two agree but for a non-empty string and an empty `t` (inside `Lowering.splitExcepted`), which `Profile.duckdb` keeps as the reference's: the lowering writes `if t = '' then s else split_part(s, t, 1)` and never reaches `split_part` there (ruling 290, `Lowering.split_native_not_excepted`).

provenance.notes: 14 rows compared with a model of Text.splitFirst: non-ASCII text and needles, several and overlapping occurrences (the leftmost wins), a needle at the start, pattern metacharacters, an absent needle, one longer than s, the empty s, the whole string, NULLs: 0 mismatches. Eight rows with an empty t (first characters of three and four bytes, U+00E9 as one code point, e followed by U+0301, one character, the empty s, a NULL s, a NULL t) compared with the first code point: 0 mismatches.
